subject: RFI: phased-shift plan + data egress & residency controls
messages:
From: Jared O'Neill <jared.oneill@starlightbank.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@starlightbank.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:14:02 -0700
Subject: RFI follow-up: implementation sequencing & data egress/residency ask

Evelyn,

Thanks for the quick RFI packet — security flagged two areas that need more color before we can move to procurement: a) a concrete phased migration / traffic-shift plan that demonstrates no uncontrolled data egress during canaries and b) a clear statement of where customer data may reside during each stage (cache, KV-store, logs). We also need approved timelines for rollback and measurable acceptance criteria for each canary phase.

Can you provide a single-run plan (sequence, owners, pre-reqs, test gates, rollback windows) and note any platform features we would rely on (VPC-only control plane, egress allowlists, KMS/HSM integrations, on-prem connector requirements)?

Compliance will also want sample audit entries showing what is logged during a traffic shift and how long those logs are retained. Target: go/no-go decision by end of Q3.

Appreciate it —
Jared O'Neill
Principal, Cloud Security
Starlight Bank

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Jared O'Neill <jared.oneill@starlightbank.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 11:02:18 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI follow-up: implementation sequencing & data egress/residency ask

Hi Jared —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a concise supplement with our egress/residency controls and a proposed phased-shift runbook (attachment: Redwood_Egress_Controls_Summary_20270615.pdf). High-level summary below; the attached MAP and checklist (we'll share the XLS and checklist in the next note) contain exact commands, expected logs, and the monitoring thresholds you requested.

High-level phased plan (targeted for Private VPC deployment):
- Pre-flight (T-30d to T-7d): network peering setup, routing maps, service account & KMS key exchange, ACL allowlist, and test cert exchange. Validation: successful TLS handshake and sample inference on staging VPC.
- Smoke (T-3d): run non-production traffic through Redwood Private (no PII). Validate egress paths — all outbound egress permitted only to customer-owned IP ranges and internal S3 endpoints. Acceptance: 0 unexpected external IPs in egress flow logs; audit log snapshot attached.
- Canary (Day 0): route 5% production traffic to Redwood instances in Starlight VPC. Canary timeframe: 4 hours minimum. Monitoring gates:
  - Error rate (5xx) < 0.5% over window OR not >2x baseline
  - Token p95 latency < 1.5x baseline
  - Model output quality delta (as measured by your prompt set evaluations) within agreed threshold (we'll capture a 50-sample eval every 30 minutes)
  - No data written to non-customer egress endpoints (automated check)

If gates pass, ramp to 25% (24–48 hours) then 60% (48–72 hours) with the same gates and progressively stricter SLOs. Full cutover planned after stability period and executive sign-off.

Rollback/stop conditions (automated + manual):
- Automated: any of the monitoring gates fail (see thresholds) triggers immediate traffic revert to the prior endpoint within 90s via our routing policy.
- Manual: CS + SRE + Customer on-call must sign off either to continue or to trigger a controlled rollback. Expected full rollback to prior state in under 15 minutes for session-less flows; for stateful connectors (mirror reads) we provide backfill guidance.

Audit & logging:
- Per-request metadata logged (request id, route id, model id, timestamp, source IP) and pushed to your customer-owned logging bucket.
- Retention: default 90d in staging; for enterprise customers we support 365d and can integrate with your SIEM via Kinesis/Logstash.

Security features relied upon: VPC-only control plane with egress allowlists, customer-managed KMS (HSM option), prefix/KV caching that is namespace-isolated and encrypted at rest, and optional on-prem connector for sensitive workloads.

I'll also attach a one-page Canary Validation Checklist that lists the exact Prometheus/trace queries we run and the log entries you'll see.

Next step: propose a 60-minute kickoff with SRE, CS, and your security team so we can finalize the MAP and sign the SLA addendum. Suggested slots next week: Tue/Wed morning PT.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Egress_Controls_Summary_20270615.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

From: Jared O'Neill <jared.oneill@starlightbank.com>

Subject: Re: RFI follow-up: implementation sequencing & data egress/residency ask

Evelyn —

This is helpful and much appreciated. A couple of clarifications before we schedule the kickoff:
1) Our compliance team requires a documented maximum window for state reconciliation when rolling back (for example, how long a partial write may persist in the event of a rollback). Please provide worst-case times for backfill or compensating sync operations.
2) Can you confirm the format of the audit entries we’ll receive (schema) and whether they include token-level hashes vs raw token values? We need to ensure no raw tokens leave our environment.
3) Timeline: we are working toward an internal deadline of 2027-09-30 for production acceptance. Can you propose a milestone plan that maps your phases to calendar dates and owner names?

If you can get those three bullets into the MAP spreadsheet we can run a quick internal review. Procurement also asked for a sample DocuSign link for the SLA addendum.

Regards,
Jared

Subject: Internal: Starlight MAP draft and owners (confidential)

Evelyn / Marissa —

Drafting the MAP workbook now (attached: MAP_Starlight_MAY2027.xlsx). Key runbook excerpts below to answer Jared's bullets and to make the client-facing MAP explicit:

State reconciliation / backfill windows:
- Stateless inference: rollback is instantaneous for routing — no backfill required.
- Stateful connectors (example: audit index writes into Starlight's Elasticsearch): we run writes to a customer-owned "mirror" index during canary. If rollback occurs, mirror is authoritative and we provide a backfill job that replays been-accepted events; worst-case replay time depends on volume. For typical Starlight peak volume (estimate 120 req/s) worst-case full backfill for 7 days of events on a 4-node job: ~10–14 hours. We'll provide a sizing doc in the map.

Audit schema (sample):
- event_time, request_id, route_id, model_version, src_ip, dst_ip, user_id_hash, token_hash, action (inference_start/inference_end), latency_ms, response_digest_hash
- We never emit raw token text; token-level data is hashed before export. Full schema attached in column F of the MAP workbook.

Milestone calendar (proposed):
- Week 0 (2027-07-05): Kickoff, finalize network & KMS keys, DocuSign SLA addendum signed. Owner: Evelyn (Redwood), Jared (Starlight).
- Week 1 (2027-07-12): Pre-flight completion (VPC peering, routing). Owner: Marissa.
- Week 2 (2027-07-19): Smoke tests + audit snapshot. Owner: SRE lead (TBD).
- Week 3 (2027-08-02): Canary 5% -> monitor 72h. Owner: Ben (CS).
- Week 6 (2027-08-23): Ramp to 60% -> 7 day stability. Owner: Ben + Starlight Ops.
- Week 10 (2027-09-27): Full cutover target if all gates green. Owner: Executive sponsors.

Attachments included in our draft: canary-validation-checklist.md (explicit queries + thresholds) and a sample DocuSign template for the SLA addendum. I'll add the worst-case backfill sizing table to the MAP before we share with Jared.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
